analyst_view.overall: Manchester City are 7th on 9 points but drew 1-1 at home to Fulham on Saturday, four Premier League games without a win and nine straight without a clean sheet. Enzo Maresca has only a short injury list: Semenyo is out (already counted), Matheus Nunes is a doubt and Khusanov played through a knock, with Enzo Fernandez expected back in midfield. Napoli, 27th on 3 points, beat Torino 1-0, but Vergara went off with a new thigh injury and may not play again this year; Allegri called the City game very important but said Napoli's fate will be decided by Club Brugge, Sabah and Viking, although he had tried to save De Bruyne for this trip. Lobotka, Meret and Di Lorenzo are out (the numbers count Lobotka and Di Lorenzo). No referee has been named.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals and already take off for Semenyo, Di Lorenzo and Lobotka. City keep conceding, and Allegri openly treats this as the less important game, so Napoli may rest players, though he did try to keep De Bruyne fresh for it. That makes me lean only a touch higher than before: 3.3 x 1.02, about 3.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with City around 6.7, and they already add about 10% for how many corners Napoli have been conceding. An Allegri side that defends deep in a back five gives up corners, but that is already in their record. I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, with Napoli's higher recent count counted (+12%). Neither side has a suspension, City's doubts are all fitness ones, and no referee has been named. I stay at 3.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.6 shots and already add about 13% to City for the volume Napoli have been allowing. Without Vergara, and with Allegri's priorities elsewhere, Napoli are likely to sit even deeper and leave City more of the ball. I go a little higher: 28.6 x 1.02, about 29.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, including Napoli's sharp recent finishing (+8%). City had only 3 on target against Fulham, which the numbers' form count partly reflects, so I keep the size small; a deeper, possibly rotated Napoli still points slightly up, to about 10.6.

note: No estimate: Champions League teams come from different leagues, and their numbers can't be compared reliably yet. Full stats appear here after the match.
